A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same M3-JEPA research work despite the revised title and terminology. The complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original multimodal retrieval, ImageNet classification, VQA, ablation and retrieval-timing results.

after.justification: v5 retains those original experiments and reports additional expert-count/top-k ablations, timing results and a VQA failure case.

M1.justification: Both versions already depict two MoE loss branches and alternating directional training. v5 reformulates routing through modality-specific experts and shared gating. Its contrastive Equation 10 also replaces v4 Equation 6's cross-pair denominator with matched-pair terms despite still describing in-batch negatives. The PDFs do not resolve whether these differences represent procedural changes or errors introduced during reformulation.

E1.justification: The same retrieval, classification and vision-language-understanding datasets and tasks remain: COCO, Flickr30K, Clotho, AudioCaps, ImageNet-1K, VQAv2 and NLVR-2. Both appendices specify matching audio-training mixtures involving WavText5K and Freesound. The added analyses reuse this coverage.

E2.justification: v5 Table 1 adds TinyCLIP and MobileCLIP to vision-language retrieval comparisons. Section 5.6 adds BLIP-2 to the timing comparison previously containing CLIP. Other benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged; X-VLM and SimVLM already appeared in v4 despite lacking their later citations.

E3.justification: v5 Appendix B.2 introduces reported sweeps over 2/8/12 experts using VQAv2 validation accuracy and top-k values 2/4/6 using Flickr30K/COCO R@1. Retained benchmark splits and metrics match. Newly supplied optimizer and learning-rate specifications do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v5 adds expert-count/top-k sensitivity studies and a VQA failure case examining missed staircase details. The main MoE, alternating-training, encoder-finetuning and loss-weight analyses remain. v4 Appendix B.1's qualitative comparison of random, adaptive and sequential task selection is no longer reported.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests. Results remain point estimates; the new parameter-statistics table concerns model sizes rather than statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: The proposed method's main results in Tables 1–4 are unchanged. Tables 5–6 replace reference-row R@1 values 88.1/90.1 with 87.7/89.7 and revise accompanying recalls; v5 newly identifies these ablations as COCO, so this is not an established same-setting performance decline. Additional results include lightweight baselines, appendix ablations, the failure case, BLIP-2's 0.05-second latency and uncached encoder timings.

T1.justification: v5 Sections 4.2–4.3 add an optimal-alpha derivation, a free-energy argument and a convergence claim assuming independent, convex, optimally solved subtasks. v4 contains the information-theoretic objective and alternating updates but lacks these derivations and convergence conditions. This substantially expands the formal argument.

C1.justification: The broad alignment, generalization and computational-efficiency claims remain. v5 newly highlights convergence and optimal-hyperparameter analysis, strengthens the claim that generalized any-to-any JEPA frameworks were previously absent, and drops v4's modality-agnostic contribution label. Appendix C explicitly qualifies that generality.

C2.justification: v5 adds substantive qualifications concerning uncached latency, audio-data sampling sensitivity, manual encoder/expert/training changes for new modalities and unexplored joint-optimization alternatives. Its VQA case study attributes missed details to simple concatenation and dominant-object focus. These materially expand v4's generation, modality-scaling and VQA limitations.

D1.justification: v5 newly specifies LoRA rank 64, batch size 128, Adam/cosine scheduling, warmup, weight decay and task-specific learning-rate endpoints, and replaces the anonymous code link with a named GitHub link. It omits v4's load-balancing-loss decision, 3,129-answer candidate count, task-specific encoder details and frozen DINOv2/CLIP linear-probing description. Reproducibility documentation changes substantially without establishing corresponding experimental changes.

R1.justification: v5 substantially develops positioning against prior MMoE, LIMoE and VL-MoE, connects its theory to COMPLETER and additional optimization literature, and expands the modality-collapse and energy-based-model motivation. These substantive relationships extend beyond the numerous publication-year and bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The introduction, methodology, theory, related work, conclusion and limitations undergo extensive rewriting. v5 adds a Preliminary section and Impact Statement, reorganizes dataset/implementation appendices and standardizes M3-JEPA, multi-gate and regularization-loss terminology. This is substantial narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: Both central framework diagrams are redrawn, and v4's separate cross-embedding figure disappears as a standalone display. The similarity heatmap moves from appendix Figure 5 to main-text Figure 3. v5 adds Tables 7–10 and a VQA example image, expands Table 1 and changes display placement while retaining the two-column template.

improvement.justification: v5 adds useful exposition, training specifications, targeted analyses and practical limitations, and makes Tables 5–6's reference rows agree with Table 1's COCO results. However, its contrastive formula conflicts with the stated negative sampling, Table 9 does not consistently support the claimed k=4 optimality, and the new alpha argument does not establish an optimum from the weighted loss. Important task-specific details also disappear. These gains and reliability problems prevent a confident net-quality judgment.
